stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Drama swirls around OpenAI’s legendary mathematical milestone
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: OpenAI claims to have found a solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem.
This mathematical problem has been unsolved for approximately 90 years.
The announcement was made via a blog post and has been covered by major outlets like The New York Times and Wired.

stories.title: Top chipmakers embrace ASML’s $400M machines, agree to crucial chipmaking change
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Major chipmakers are adopting new ASML lithography machines.
The industry has agreed to a crucial change in chip manufacturing processes.
This change is projected to boost the productivity of the new ASML machines by 40%.

stories.title: Large language models develop novel social biases through adaptive exploration
stories.author: paimapi
bullet_points: LLMs are demonstrating the development of novel social biases.
This bias emerges as a result of the models' adaptive exploration processes.
The finding highlights a critical, emergent risk in advanced AI systems.

stories.title: AlphaGenome Atlas: a high-resolution map of human DNA
stories.author: utiiiD
bullet_points: DeepMind has released the AlphaGenome Atlas, a high-resolution predictive map of the human DNA.
The atlas aims to predict the effects of every possible DNA letter change within the human genome.
This represents a significant advancement in computational biology and genomics, leveraging advanced AI.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary function as a generative AI.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, suggesting a focus on model deployment and comparison.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to the transformer architecture and the Llama family of models.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It indicates the model is being used for text-generation tasks.
The associated tags point to key technologies like transformers, safetensors, and the Llama architecture.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local, self-hosted execution, supporting multi-step tasks and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.31 significantly boosts Gemma 4 performance on Apple Silicon.
The speedup is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Performance saw up to 90% improvement when used with coding agents on the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents entirely on local, personal hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: ChatGPT Sketch turns your bad drawings into detailed AI images
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: OpenAI has introduced 'Sketch' within ChatGPT Images 2.5.
Users can now generate detailed AI images by providing a simple hand-drawn doodle as input.
This feature enhances the multimodal capabilities of ChatGPT by accepting rough sketches as prompts.

stories.title: Meta bets on AI agent Muse to catch up in AI race
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Meta is heavily investing in its AI strategy with the launch of Muse, a personal AI assistant.
Muse is positioned as a tool designed to make advanced AI accessible to a broad user base.
This initiative is part of a larger, multi-billion dollar effort by Meta to improve its competitive standing in the AI sector.

stories.title: “This is the AI men actually use”: Meta ads pushed apps nudifying real teens
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Meta was criticized for delaying the removal of advertisements on Instagram.
These ads were found to be nudifying or altering photos of young girls.
The story highlights ongoing ethical concerns regarding AI/algorithmic influence on minors' social media use.

stories.title: Same Trajectory, Contradictory Rewards (ROBORMBENCH): Paraphrase Fragility in Vision Language Reward Models
stories.author: Albert No
bullet_points: Current Vision-Language Models (VLMs) used as reward functions for robotic learning often lack paraphrase invariance.
Minor changes in goal description (paraphrasing) can drastically alter the predicted reward score for the same robot trajectory.
This fragility poses a significant reliability risk for deploying VLM-based reinforcement learning systems in real-world robotics.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models and hardware.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting users on Apple silicon.

stories.title: AI power users claim Anthropic duped them with subscriptions, and they’re taking it to court
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: Anthropic is facing a class action lawsuit from AI power users.
The core claim is that Anthropic misled subscribers regarding the value of its top-tier pricing.
The dispute arises despite Anthropic claiming power users are central to its business strategy.

stories.title: Tesla Cybercab doesn’t have any manual controls — but it does have a virtual joystick
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: The Tesla Cybercab is designed without traditional manual controls like a steering wheel or pedals.
Initial reports suggested the vehicle was entirely autonomous.
However, riders have since discovered hidden or secret manual controls within the Cybercab.

stories.title: ProcArena: A Multi-Scenario Benchmark for LLMs on Direct and Interactive PL/SQL Development from Natural Language
stories.author: Pengcheng Ge
bullet_points: Introduces ProcArena, a new benchmark specifically designed to test LLMs on PL/SQL development.
Addresses a gap in current research by moving beyond simple NL-to-PL/SQL generation to cover complex, real-world scenarios.
The benchmark covers diverse development tasks, including from-scratch coding, code modification, debugging, and optimization.

stories.title: One MLLM, One Call: Efficient Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation via Spatial-Aware Waypoints
stories.author: Xu Wang
bullet_points: Introduces O2C-Nav, a new framework for Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN-CE) in continuous environments.
Addresses the high inference latency and computational overhead of existing zero-shot VLN methods.
Achieves efficiency by requiring only a single large model call per decision step, unlike previous multi-query approaches.

stories.title: Causal Attribution for Agentic Decisions: Estimators, Coupling, and a Traceability Specification
stories.author: Ajay Pravin Mahale
bullet_points: Addresses the critical, unresolved issue of causal attribution for decisions made by complex, agentic AI systems.
Proposes a novel estimator framework to isolate the specific contribution of individual steps within an AI decision-making process.
Establishes necessary conditions for traceability in high-risk AI systems, differentiating between marginal and common-random-numbers total effects.

stories.title: Collision Snapshot Guided Time-Reversed Safety-Critical Scenario Generation
stories.author: Jongeun Choi
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of generating realistic, safety-critical scenarios for autonomous vehicle training.
Current methods, which rely on perturbing existing trajectories with simplified adversarial objectives, suffer from limited plausibility and diversity.
The proposed method, 'Collision Snapshot Guided Time-Reversed Scenario Generation,' aims to improve scenario generation by intelligently introducing new adversarial vehicles.

stories.title: On BatchNorm Forward Modes in Value-Based Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Koustuv Sinha
bullet_points: Investigates the impact of Batch Normalization (BN) in Value-Based Reinforcement Learning (RL).
Addresses a reported performance degradation of BN in discrete-action Atari RL, contrary to its success in continuous control.
Proposes that selectively choosing between running and batch statistics during specific forward passes can resolve this degradation in target-based and target-free Q-networks.

stories.title: From Concentration to Differentiation and Back: Routing Effective Rank in MoE Reasoning Cohorts
stories.author: Yu-Gang Jiang
bullet_points: Introduces 'routing effective rank' (deff) to quantify the internal computation reorganization in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models during inference.
Demonstrates that deff exhibits a reproducible low-high-low trajectory across various MoE configurations and benchmarks.
This research provides a label-free method to analyze how MoE reasoning cohorts change as inference progresses, suggesting a dynamic computational structure.

stories.title: Building Trustworthy Graph-Agentic RAG for Social Good: Architectures, Failure Propagation, and Assurance by Construction
stories.author: Raviteja Bommireddy
bullet_points: Introduces Graph-Agentic RAG, an advanced architecture combining structured evidence with adaptive planning controllers.
This system excels in complex scenarios requiring relational reasoning across multiple documents, entities, or timeframes.
Highlights a critical challenge: coupled failure paths where errors in graph construction can propagate through the system to consequential outcomes.

stories.title: Not Just Oversmoothing: Detecting the Echo Chamber Effect in Graph Neural Networks
stories.author: Saman Halgamuge
bullet_points: The paper addresses the limitations of current diagnostics for Graph Neural Network (GNN) failure modes, specifically oversmoothing.
It proposes a new perspective recognizing that GNN message passing operates on distinct timescales (fast within communities, slow across them).
The research aims to detect the 'Echo Chamber Effect' by capturing heterogeneous dynamics within community structures, which existing global measures miss.

stories.title: Structural Entropy-Driven Graph Diffusion Generation for One-Shot Federated Graph Learning
stories.author: Chuan Chen
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of one-shot Federated Graph Learning (FGL) where server estimates must be made from compressed client data.
Proposes SPIRE, a Structural Entropy-Driven Graph Diffusion Generation method to introduce topology-aware client differentiation.
Uses first-order degree-distribution structural entropy to move beyond simple volume-based weighting of client contributions.

stories.title: OracleZoom: On-Policy Self-Distillation Inspired Reference-Constrained Recursive Image Super Resolution
stories.author: Nobin Sarwar
bullet_points: Introduces OracleZoom, a novel framework for Recursive Super-Resolution (SR) to handle extreme magnification.
Addresses the challenge of lacking ground truth data at deeper, higher-resolution scales in recursive SR.
Utilizes an on-policy distillation-inspired, reference-constrained training approach.

stories.title: WearableQA: A Benchmark for Health Reasoning over Real-World Wearable Data
stories.author: Benoit Corda
bullet_points: Introduces WearableQA, a new benchmark designed to test AI reasoning over real-world, longitudinal wearable data.
The benchmark utilizes complex, authentic datasets from 200 users, including time series, blood biomarkers, and demographics.
Addresses a gap in current research by moving beyond simple signal processing to evaluate higher-level health reasoning capabilities of AI systems.

stories.title: Multi-Step Tool-Calling over Korean Open Public APIs: A Benchmark and a Data-Synthesis Recipe
stories.author: Kyuseong Lim
bullet_points: Addresses a critical industry need: deploying on-premise, open-source LLM agents for government APIs due to data-sovereignty regulations.
Introduces KOPA-Bench, a new benchmark with 145 real-world tasks specifically designed to measure multi-step tool-calling performance in Korean public APIs.
Proposes EDGE, a novel data synthesis technique (Execution-grounded Dynamic Graph) to improve performance in complex tool-calling scenarios.

stories.title: Does Your Agent's Memory Survive a Model Upgrade? A Controlled Study of Memory Portability
stories.author: Jaideep Ray
bullet_points: Investigates the critical issue of memory portability when upgrading large language models (LLMs).
Identifies that preserving raw memory history is insufficient; model interpretation and embedding versions affect retrieval.
Compares different memory storage methods (LC-RAW, RAG chunks, NOTES, normalized) to assess upgrade resilience.

stories.title: Large Language Models for HVAC Operations in Building Energy Systems: A Critical Review of Methods, Applications, and Deployment Readiness
stories.author: Martin Kriegel
bullet_points: The review addresses the challenge of extracting insights from rich but unstructured building automation sensor data.
It systematically analyzes 66 peer-reviewed studies on using Large Language Models (LLMs) specifically for HVAC operations.
The research assesses the maturity of these applications based on evidence realism and deployment readiness.

stories.title: Can Large Language Models Anticipate Behavioral Responses to Social Policies? A Case of Pension Enrollment Prediction among China's Flexible Workers
stories.author: Runhuan Feng
bullet_points: Proposes using Large Language Models (LLMs) as novel tools for policy assessment, addressing limitations of traditional econometric methods.
Introduces FlexPension-LLM, a domain-specialized LLM designed for hierarchical pension enrollment prediction.
Focuses on a practical application: predicting behavioral responses to social policy changes among China's flexible workers.

stories.title: Muse – Meta’s personal AI agent
stories.author: yks
bullet_points: Meta is developing 'Muse,' a personal AI agent.
The announcement is featured on Hacker News, indicating tech community interest.
The specific capabilities of Muse are not detailed in the provided content.

stories.title: Benchmarking Qwen3.8 27B quantizations: 4-bit holds up, 1-bit collapses
stories.author: stared
bullet_points: The article benchmarks different quantization levels (4-bit vs. 1-bit) for the Qwen3.8 27B model.
The findings indicate that 4-bit quantization maintains performance, while 1-bit quantization leads to significant performance degradation.
This is relevant to the ongoing trend of optimizing large language models for efficient deployment on consumer or edge hardware.

stories.title: Most 'AI Agents' Are Just If-Statements in a Trench Coat
stories.author: james_anderson_h
bullet_points: Critiques the current state of 'AI Agents,' suggesting many are overhyped.
Argues that many existing agents are functionally limited, resembling complex 'if-statements.'
Highlights the gap between the perceived capability of AI agents and their actual underlying complexity.

stories.title: Why I built a zero-telemetry Chrome extension to measure the physical cost of AI prompts
stories.author: ib2mofficial
bullet_points: The article discusses the growing reliance of developers on Large Language Models (LLMs).
The author built a zero-telemetry Chrome extension to track the physical cost associated with AI prompts.
This addresses the often-unseen environmental or operational costs of using generative AI tools.
